statement: A rhombus has diagonals of length 10 and 24. What is its perimeter?

choices.misconception: I found the length of one side and forgot to multiply by four.
I added the two diagonals and doubled, as if they were the sides.
I used the whole diagonals, 10 and 24, as the legs of the right triangle, which gave a side of 26.
I found the area, half of 10 × 24, instead of the perimeter.

hints: What do the diagonals of a rhombus do to each other?
The diagonals of a rhombus cut each other in half at right angles, splitting the rhombus into four equal right triangles. Each side of the rhombus is the longest side of one of them.
Each right triangle has legs 5 and 12, half of each diagonal.

solutions.reliable: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so they split it into four right triangles with legs 5 and 12. Each side of the rhombus is the hypotenuse: the square root of 25 + 144 = 169, which is 13. The perimeter is 4 × 13 = 52. The transferable idea: in a rhombus, half of each diagonal and a side form a right triangle.

whyOnTest: Quadrilateral-property questions check that you know a rhombus's diagonals bisect at right angles; using whole diagonals is the classic slip.
